canonical_candidate.title: MunTTS: A Text-to-Speech System for Mundari
canonical_candidate.publication: Proceedings of the Seventh Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages

exact_locator_evidence.support: Study scope is Mundari spoken in Jharkhand and written in Devanagari; paper reports 15,656 unique sentences, 26,868 audio recordings, 27.51 hours, male and female voices.
Karya reports Mundari speakers were reached in 15 villages; 60,000 Hindi sentences were translated into Mundari; two speakers, one man and one woman, were selected to record the corpus.

rights_access.acl_paper: publicly accessible through ACL Anthology; paper copyright line is Association for Computational Linguistics (2024)
rights_access.dataset: do not infer redistribution permission from public descriptions; dataset license/version must be verified independently before ingestion or exposure

provenance_uncertainty: Paper reports 26,868 recordings; repository/release count previously observed as 26,870 remains a version-lineage discrepancy and must not be silently normalized.
Karya case-study statement of 60,000 translated Hindi sentences is not equivalent to the paper's 15,656 unique-sentence TTS subset.
Two-speaker recording provenance does not by itself establish participant/community consent for downstream redistribution or cultural reuse.
No cultural proposition is promoted from a computational speech corpus.
note: Audit enrichment only. Never use this file to imply controlled-count promotion.
